# The Age of Discontinuity: Guidelines to Our Changing Society

Image: Front CoverPeter DruckerRoutledge, 2017 - Business & Economics - 434 pages The closing decades of the twentieth century have been characterized as a period of disruption and discontinuity in which the structure and meaning of economy, polity, and society have been radically altered. In this volume Peter Drucker focuses with great clarity and perception on the forces of change that are transforming the economic landscape and creating tomorrow's society. Drucker discerns four major areas of discontinuity underlying contemporary social and cultural reality. These are: (1) the explosion of new technologies resulting in major new industries; (2) the change from an international to a world economy an economy that presently lacks policy, theory, and institutions; (3) a new sociopolitical reality of pluralistic institutions that poses drastic political, philosophical, and spritual challenges; and (4) the new universe of knowledge based on mass education and its implications in work, leisure, and leadership. Peter Drucker brings to this work an intimate knowledge and objective view of the particular and general. The Age of Discontinuity is a fascinating and important blueprint for shaping a future already very much with us.

# The Age of Discontinuity: Guidelines to Our Changing Society

Peter F. DruckerElsevier, Oct 22, 2013 - Social Science - 380 pages The Age of Discontinuity: Guidelines to Our Changing Society describes the discontinuities that are changing the structure and the meaning of economy, politics, and society. Major discontinuities exist in four areas: the knowledge technologies; changes in the world's economy; a society of organizations; and the knowledge society. This book is organized into four parts encompassing 17 chapters. Each part represents the four areas of discontinuities. Part I highlights the growth in major industries and businesses, along with economic policies related to tax incentives. Part II looks into the status of the global economy, the disparity between the rich and poor countries, and the concepts and application of the economic theory demonstrating a closed economy controlled from within by national, monetary, credit, and tax policies. Part III examines the changes in the political matrix of social and economic life. This part deals particularly with the theory of pluralism and organizations, as well as the creation of socio-political reality. Part IV focuses on the changes in the cost center and the crucial resource of the economy. Knowledge changes involve changes in labor forces and work. This book will prove useful to economists, public servants, sociologists, and researchers. [Input]

# The Engineering Book: Big Ideas Simply Explained

Image: Front CoverDK Publishing (Dorling Kindersley), Mar 23, 2027 - Technology & Engineering - 336 pages How did the ancient Egyptians build the pyramids? What makes a suspension bridge so strong? An why do some machines revolutionize society while others fade into obscurity?
Discover all of the most important ideas and groundbreaking developments that have shaped the world of civil and mechanical engineering in The Engineering Book. From the wonders of ancient construction to the innovations defining modern infrastructure, this comprehensive guide explores and explains more than 90 of the most pivotal concepts in a clear and accessible way. Featuring dynamic graphics, engaging explanations, and insights into the minds behind the most iconic projects, this book delves into everything from structural integrity and earthquake resilience to hydrology and green engineering. Find out how bridges stand tall, how tunnels are carved through mountains, and the ways in which modern cities thrive on sustainable design. Perfect for students, aspiring engineers and architects, and anyone who is curious about the built world, The Engineering Book sheds light on the principles that shape our lives, from everyday utilities to awe-inspiring megastructures.
